title: New Pixel Phones Betting on AI to Tempt Buyers
paragraphs: Google has unveiled its latest Pixel smartphones, and once again, the company is relying heavily on artificial intelligence to persuade consumers to upgrade.

The new lineup was announced on August 12, 2026, and customers in the United States were able to start ordering the devices that same day. It consists of four phones: the Pixel 11, the Pixel 11 Pro, the Pixel 11 Pro XL and the foldable Pixel Pro Fold. In the US, they cost $900, $1,100, $1,300 and $1,900 respectively, which represents an increase of $100 for each model compared with the previous year. However, Google has also discontinued the cheapest 128GB version of the base model, which previously sold for $800, so storage now starts at 256GB, double the previous amount.

In terms of hardware, the phones feature slimmer cameras with more powerful zoom, a battery life of up to 30 hours and faster wireless charging. Nevertheless, it is the software that Google is emphasizing most. One new feature, called Magic Capture, takes a series of photos and a video with a single tap of the shutter button. The phones can also extract still photos from videos, stabilize footage and act as a teleprompter. In addition, speech-to-text has been improved, and the devices can now provide live translation of videos, podcasts and voice messages. Buyers of the Pro and Pro XL models will also receive a free six-month subscription to Google's AI Pro service.
Google also introduced a tracking device called the Pixel Tag, which costs $30 for one or $100 for a pack of four.

Google has been steadily adding AI features to its Pixel phones since 2023. Even so, the phones remain considerably less popular than Apple's iPhone. Interestingly, Apple announced in June that it would improve its own AI features using Google's Gemini model, a move that many observers see as a sign that Apple has been struggling to keep up in the field.

According to Andrew Cornwall, a senior analyst at the research firm Forrester, Google continues to promote mainly AI-driven software features as the main reason for consumers to buy a new phone. Whether shoppers will be convinced, however, remains to be seen.
